description: The true path of the miniature: a witness saw a figure and took it for a man she knew by his cloak; what she saw is kept, her identification is set aside, and the cloak leads to who wore it.

moves.why: The doctor was at the Squire's bedside at nine: I sat beside him.

moves.see: she knew the figure by the cloak
moves.why: Mrs. Lunn knew him by the cloak, in the dark.
She saw a figure in a cloak; that it was the doctor is what she made of it, and it cannot be so.
Her mistake is itself worth having: somebody passed for the doctor.
He wore his greatcoat that night.

moves.see: someone else wore it in the rain
moves.why: And the cloak he left at home was damp in the morning.

moves.see: could let themselves out at the side door
moves.why: Whoever came out at the side door had a key to it.
The cloak hung clear of the ground.

moves.see: on Kitty it would have trailed
moves.why: Kitty is hardly five feet tall.
